business_rules.statement: The Command Center is the cockpit, never the engine. It owns no record; there is no separate Command Center database.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Static persistence-dependency assertion across all Command Center modules; build fails if one is introduced

business_rules.statement: Every Command Center action is a command against a DOH-owned record, executed through the owning DOH service, written to the DOH audit trail; the set is a closed list of ten and adding an action is a scope decision, never a drift.

Rule one — nothing crosses a seam without a defined envelope or contract. Captures cross with the runtime envelope; operational events with the lighter envelope; commands as one of five classes; content as a version-pinned work package. There is no informal crossing.
Rule two — every flow is one-directional per record type. A reader's action does not flow back as a record change; it flows back as a command through the owning service.
The Frontline Worker Application is the only surface in the platform where operational data is created; no operational data originates in the DOH itself.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Absence of any capture-creating control on Hub, Studio, Command Center and console surfaces

business_rules.statement: No back-office data entry, no import path for operational data, and no synthesis by the platform. The platform never invents content, rules, or thresholds.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Import path rejection of operational record types; TEST-ORIGIN-001/002/003

business_rules.statement: Missing data is recorded as missing with its reason and is never filled in. Corrections are append-only and the original capture is always readable.
The audit log is immutable and append-only; an action that cannot be audited does not happen. No surface and no role can mutate the audit log.
A cell in either permission view is never blank; it carries a status from the closed set. Unavailable and Explicitly prohibited are different statements and must never be merged.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Generator consistency gate at build time

business_rules.statement: A functionality with no row for one of the nine role types fails the build, because an unstated permission is an undefined permission.
Access is an intersection of nine conditions evaluated at once; if any one says no, the answer is no; if any says never, the answer is never even if all the others said yes.
Explicit deny wins: where any condition produces an explicit deny, the request is refused regardless of how many conditions produced an allow.

Safety controls win: where a safety control conflicts with any other condition, including a root-level allow, the safety control decides. Safety controls are evaluated first and cannot be reordered by configuration.
The decision and its audit event commit in one transaction; an action that cannot be audited does not occur. Where the audit writer cannot commit, the action does not happen.
Deny-by-default: an unresolved or unreachable permission condition produces a refusal, never a grant. An absolute rule that cannot be evaluated is treated as violated.
A refusal caused by a scope miss does not disclose the existence of the out-of-scope object.
Cached decisions serve reads only and always render a freshness marker naming the decision's age. Write paths never use a cached decision.

An action bound to one named role type is allowed only when that role type is held; no union of other roles substitutes for it. Scope is taken from the role type that produced the allow, never from the union of all scopes held.
The audit log records the user identity and the action, never an acting-as-role fiction; the deciding role type is recorded as a decision input only.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Audit schema — no acting-as-role field exists

business_rules.statement: There are exactly three named access classes and only three: the normal support session, the compliance-emergency path, and the JBS access grant. No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Console gateway; every tenant-content read path

business_rules.statement: A normal support session is read-only without exception; no write capability exists inside it. A data repair is not support.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Session service refuses every write verb

business_rules.statement: The compliance-emergency path is the only class with write capability into tenant data and the only entry into a compliance-suspended tenant, and requires two authorisations, the root and one Admin, with scope declared before the session opens.
business_rules.applies_to: tenant data writes by platform staff

business_rules.statement: Every cross-boundary access is written twice: once in the platform audit and once mirrored into the tenant's audit stream, in the same transaction. If the mirror write fails, the session action is refused.

No tenant record is read while the tenant cannot see that it is being read; if the banner cannot render, the session is suspended and no further reads are served until the banner is confirmed visible.
Employment by JBS, by the client, or by an implementation partner never confers permanent access. Every crossing is granted, exercised, and expires.
Absolute rule 1 — There is no Tenant Super Admin. No role exists inside a tenant workspace above the Tenant Admin, and none may be created.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Tenant role catalogue, fixed at five

business_rules.statement: Absolute rule 3 — The Tenant Admin has no automatic platform authority; no emergency creates the path.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Console authentication and the domain boundary

business_rules.statement: Absolute rules 4-8 — Exactly one Root Super Admin account, created through the backend at commissioning; not clonable, not shareable, not convertible from a Tenant Admin, not assignable by a Tenant Admin.

Absolute rule 11 — The six platform invariants (evaluation gate, sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, cross-tenant analytics anonymisation, one-transaction audit guarantee) bind every account including the root and have no off position and no approval path around them.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Settings render locked; no approval path exists

business_rules.statement: Absolute rule 12 — Severity 1 lot release is Quality Manager only, uniformly. No platform role, no Tenant Admin, and no artificial-intelligence agent may release a Severity 1 hold.
Absolute rule 13 — There is no self-registration and no password-only path on the console, and no role-escalation path except the root acting.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Console authentication and the Users pane

business_rules.statement: Absolute rule 14 — At least one Tenant Admin always exists, and an approver-capable role must exist whenever a Job exists; a removal that would breach either is refused with the rule named.
An absolute-rule refusal short-circuits the remaining evaluation, names the rule in plain language rather than a numeric code, and writes a security-relevant audit event.
Tenants may make the platform stricter than default and may never make it looser than the platform floor; the platform rejects a looser-than-floor value rather than logging it.

Qualifications are supervisor-entered with a full audit trail; self-attestation is not permitted for any worker. Supervisor permission alone authorises worker-record changes; the audit trail, not a second approval, is the control.

A Supervisor clearance covers an expired certification only; a never-held qualification requires the Quality Manager; a second clearance in the same Area on the same shift, regardless of worker, routes to the Quality Manager.

The login is the credential, not the device: identity, qualifications, language preference and attribution travel with the worker onto any conformant device, and a shared tablet confers nothing by itself.
Delegation is deferred beyond V1; cover is handled by manually adding and removing the role.
No blocked action is replayed automatically on recovery, because a replayed approval is an approval nobody gave.
Exit from the ReadOnly state requires three consecutive healthy evaluations and passes through a mandatory reconciliation state before returning to healthy.
Do not create a hidden second root account as a fallback; a standing second root defeats the property that makes the root auditable. Re-provisioning is atomic replacement, never addition.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Continuous assertion that exactly one root identity is enabled

business_rules.statement: No mutating Band A change applies without an approval record naming a different approver identity; maker and checker must differ.

The evaluation gate sits before the approval cycle, not inside it: no agent, capability or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios, and no approval path exists around the gate. An unavailable harness blocks rather than waives.
No Band A change auto-applies on a timeout or in the absence of an Admin; an auto-applied change is an unapproved change.
Critical-class requests never auto-approve, expire silently, or apply without a recorded root decision; they wait and re-notify.
A successful service call is never rendered as an applied device command; a created command is not an applied command.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Command state rendering; read-back from the Hub

business_rules.statement: Exactly five tenant role types exist and no interface can create a sixth; there is no Quality Director role, and Job Owner is a field on the Job record, not a role.
Scope is limited to Tenant, Site and Area, three orthogonal dimensions held simultaneously; Location (Cell), Job and worker-level scoping are deferred beyond V1 and no rule may depend on them.

Under soft suspension, master-data writes are blocked while operations continue in full and recertification of existing workers stays open. Under compliance suspension, all logins are blocked immediately, in-flight runs stop, and devices lock at next contact with the fixed worker-facing message.

decisions.question: Do the five tenant roles form an authority ordering, such that the plus notation means 'this role and every role above it', or are they unordered and additive, such that the plus notation abbreviates an enumerated set?
options: Option 1 — declare an ordering (Worker, Supervisor, Quality Manager, Tenant Admin), reading plus as 'and above'
Option 2 — declare enumerated sets, replacing every plus form with an explicit list of role types
Option 3 — union with explicit-deny precedence, no ordering
decisions.adopted_working_position: Every authority statement is written with the explicit role types named, and no chapter assumes an ordering among the five additive tenant roles. Where a chapter reproduces a plus form quoted from the source, the reader is directed to DEC-PLUS-001 for its meaning.
decisions.status: open — recommendation (Option 3) explicitly not adopted as a requirement
decisions.impact: Blocks the final authority columns in Chapter 17 and the substitute sign-off behaviour in the Frontline Worker Application.

decisions.question: Who may substitute for a Supervisor sign-off on a worker device when no Supervisor is available, given §7.13.3's 'higher authority' clause and the absence of any hierarchy in Part III or Part IV?
options: Name the Quality Manager as the only substitute
Name the Quality Manager and the Tenant Admin
Make the substitute set a tenant configuration within a platform floor
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: the Quality Manager only. This recommendation is not adopted as a requirement.
decisions.impact: A required supervisor sign-off gates a worker's screen; no substitute stops the run, any substitute makes the gate worthless.

decisions.question: Who holds custody of the root account, who are the two break-glass custodians, what is the tolerable duration of a root outage, and what out-of-band identity verification does the client use?
options: Option A — single named custodian with a documented emergency contact
Option B — two custodians who jointly re-provision, neither holding the credential in ordinary operation
Option C — custody held by a third party under escrow
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: Option B, with a documented rehearsal cadence and a stated outage tolerance.
decisions.impact: Blocks the operational runbook, not the software; the software behaviour is settled by SoW Fact §8.8.1.

decisions.question: Whether a JBS access grant may carry write capability into tenant data.
options: Read-only always, with any write performed by client staff through the compliance-emergency path
A write-capable JBS class requiring the same dual authorisation
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: read-only always, because it keeps §8.15.2's 'only one' statement literally true.
decisions.impact: Determines whether an external party can ever alter a manufacturer's production record.

decisions.question: Whether the tenant-visible banner and the tenant's End-session control apply to the compliance-emergency path and the JBS access grant, or only to the normal support session.
options: Banner and End-session on all three
Banner on all three but no End-session on the compliance-emergency path
Banner suppressed on the compliance-emergency path entirely
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: banner on all three, End-session on the normal support session and the JBS grant but not on the compliance-emergency path, with the post-session report as compensating visibility.
decisions.impact: A tenant cannot stop an emergency session, which is deliberate and must be stated in the tenant contract.

decisions.question: Whether the root may itself act as the checker on a Platform Engineer Band A change, substituting for Admin in the maker-checker cycle.
options: The root may act as checker for continuity
The root may not, preserving a strict two-person separation
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: the root may act as checker only where no Admin account exists or all Admin accounts are disabled, recorded with an explicit continuity reason. This blueprint does not assume the root may substitute.
decisions.impact: Determines whether Band A changes stall when no Admin is available.

decisions.question: Should any class of platform access into tenant data require the Tenant Admin's affirmative approval before it opens?
options: No consent required, visibility only, as the source implies
Consent required for the normal support session with an automatic-approval timeout
Consent required for JBS grants only
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: consent required for JBS grants only, with visibility-only for the client's own support.
decisions.impact: The difference between a manufacturer being informed and being in control; materially affects support response times.

decisions.question: Whether the placement of a legal hold on a tenant's data is disclosed to that tenant.
options: Always disclose
Never disclose
Disclose unless the hold carries a non-disclosure flag set at placement
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: the third option, making non-disclosure an explicit, audited decision rather than a default.
decisions.impact: In some jurisdictions disclosure is required; in others it is prejudicial.

decisions.question: Whether a support session may be extended beyond its time box, by whom, and how many times.
options: No extension, always a new session
Extension by the engineer with a new reason, capped at one
Extension requiring an Admin
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: no extension, always a new session, so each session carries its own reason and time box.
decisions.impact: Trades support efficiency against audit clarity for long investigations.

decisions.question: Whether a support engineer may export anything from inside a session, such as a record extract attached to a ticket.
options: No export, findings written in prose only
Export of a defined minimal extract, itself audited and mirrored and listed in Platform Access History
Unrestricted export
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: no export, with findings written in prose, keeping tenant operational content inside the platform where the mirroring holds.
decisions.impact: An export removes tenant operational content into a ticketing system the tenant cannot see.

decisions.question: The lifecycle of the authoring grant and the Agent Author delegation: does an ordinary tenant authoring grant carry an expiry, require periodic re-affirmation, or get reviewed?
options: Perpetual until revoked, matching the plain reading
An expiry set at assignment
A periodic re-affirmation, for example annually, with a notification to the Tenant Admin
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: perpetual until revoked, with a mandatory annual review report listing every grant-holder.
decisions.impact: An authoring grant lets a Supervisor create content governing a factory floor; an unrevoked grant accumulates silently.

decisions.question: The Standards and Operations Studio module count: the source gives no canonical count and this blueprint derives eighteen from §5.1 through §5.18.
options: Accept the derived count of 18
Client states a canonical count
decisions.adopted_working_position: The feature-centric view must never present the derived Studio count as source-backed; it renders with a derived-count qualifier and a DEC-STUDIO-001 reference.
decisions.impact: Affects every module inventory and coverage total for the Studio surface.

decisions.question: What Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective apply to platform-side services, in particular the access decision path and the Hub record service?
options: Minutes-scale with active redundancy
Hours-scale with warm standby
Next-business-day with backup restore
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation: minutes-scale for the access decision path specifically, because it gates every surface. The Statement of Work states no availability targets.
decisions.impact: Determines redundancy cost and how long a tenant's in-shift authority may be unavailable.

decisions.question: Whether atom enablement is a Platform Engineer Band A change requiring Admin approval (§8.2.2) or an Admin action as a platform-side tenant current-value change including feature enablement (§8.19).
options: Platform Engineer submission with Admin approval
Admin action
decisions.adopted_working_position: Both readings are preserved; not resolved here.
decisions.impact: Determines who may enable a feature or atom and whether maker-checker applies.

decisions.question: What the platform does when nobody holding the target role is on shift for an escalation.
options: Fall back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift and mark the delivery as a fallback
decisions.adopted_working_position: The platform falls back to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift and marks the delivery as a fallback so the gap is visible rather than silent.
decisions.impact: Determines whether an escalation is delivered or silently dropped outside shift coverage.

decisions.question: What happens when a device wipe command targets an offline device that never returns.
decisions.impact: Unresolved terminal state for a wipe command against a permanently offline device.

decisions.question: Device storage-full behaviour when local captures cannot be committed.
decisions.impact: Affects the sole-origin guarantee when a device runs out of durable local store.

decisions.question: Whether a library edit propagating immediately to referencing screens affects an in-flight run whose package is pinned at assignment.
options: Library edit propagates to the in-flight run
The pinned package governs the in-flight run
decisions.adopted_working_position: Both readings are preserved; the interaction for an in-flight run is unstated.
decisions.impact: Determines whether workers mid-run see changed content.

decisions.question: What a role definition card export ('Save as document') may contain.
decisions.impact: Bounds what permission documentation leaves the platform.

decisions.question: The Plant Manager and Quality Director contradiction — job titles used in the source that are not platform roles.
decisions.adopted_working_position: This chapter references and does not resolve it.
decisions.impact: Determines whether additional personas map to any of the five fixed tenant roles.

contradictions.description: The plus notation (`Supervisor+`, `QM+`) implies an ordering the source never defines; §6.1.3 leans to an ordering while §4.8.4's additive statement and §3.5's flat five-role list lean to enumerated sets.
conflicting_values: Reading A: the plus form is shorthand for an ordering across the five roles
Reading B: the plus form abbreviates an enumerated set and the roles remain unordered and purely additive

contradictions.description: §7.13.3 says a 'higher authority' may sign off for an unavailable supervisor, with the hierarchy 'resolved from the Hub, within the platform's five fixed roles and the authority matrix of Part III'. Part III contains no such ordering and Part IV defines no hierarchy.
conflicting_values: §7.13.3 asserts a resolvable role hierarchy
Part III and Part IV define no hierarchy; the five roles are additive and unordered

contradictions.description: §8.16 places JBS access under 'exactly the same discipline' as the other classes while §8.15.2 says the compliance-emergency path is 'the only one with write capability'; §8.8.5 nevertheless contemplates JBS authoring capacity that writes.
conflicting_values: JBS grant is read-only (from §8.15.2's 'only one')
JBS personnel perform authoring work inside a tenant context under §8.8.5, which writes

contradictions.description: §8.2.2 makes atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval, while §8.19 makes platform-side tenant current-value changes, including feature enablement, Admin actions.
conflicting_values: Platform Engineer submission with Admin approval (§8.2.2)
Admin action (§8.19)

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work gives no canonical Standards and Operations Studio module count; the blueprint derives eighteen from §5.1 through §5.18 and forbids presenting it as source-backed.
conflicting_values: 18 modules (derived from §5.1–§5.18)
no canonical count exists in the source

contradictions.description: A library edit propagates immediately to referencing screens while a work package is pinned at run assignment; the interaction for an in-flight run is unstated and both readings are preserved.
conflicting_values: library edit propagates immediately to referencing screens
the package is pinned at assignment and governs the in-flight run

contradictions.description: The source names Job approval under the Quality Manager remit while §3.5 says separation of duties is satisfied by any second holder of the approving role; the blueprint therefore declares Supervisor Job approval Explicitly prohibited.
conflicting_values: Job approval is a Quality Manager remit (§4.8.1)
separation of duties is satisfied by any second holder of the approving role (§3.5)

contradictions.description: §8.8.3 names Admin as the approver for Platform Engineer changes and separately says the critical class escalates to the root; whether the root may itself act as checker is unstated.
conflicting_values: the root may act as checker for continuity
the root may not, preserving strict two-person separation

contradictions.description: §8.15.1 attaches the tenant banner and End-session control explicitly to the normal support session and says nothing about the compliance-emergency path or the JBS grant.
conflicting_values: banner and End-session on all three classes
banner/End-session only on the normal support session

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work describes the root account as having 'unrestricted access to both bands' and then immediately constrains it with the six invariants, the evaluation gate, and the three named access classes.
conflicting_values: 'unrestricted access to both bands' (§8.8.1)
the six platform invariants, the evaluation gate, and the three-layer access boundary bind it (§8.8.1, §3.1, §8.1.2, §8.15)

contradictions.description: The Statement of Work uses job titles that are not platform roles — quality engineer, manufacturing engineer, Plant Manager, Quality Director, implementation team, JBS delivery staff — while fixing exactly five tenant roles.
conflicting_values: personas named in the source (Plant Manager, Quality Director, quality engineer)
exactly five fixed tenant roles, no Quality Director role

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A surface accumulates a persisted artefact it may not own — typically a cache that grew into a store, or a convenience table
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Remove the artefact and route the capability through the owning service
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If removal is not possible within the release, the capability is withdrawn
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prohibited artefact does not exist
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Data held only in the prohibited artefact is migrated into the owning service through an audited import preserving original timestamps and attribution, annotated as reconstructed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A flow stalls at a seam: package build, upload, command delivery, agent proposal, or summary computation
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry with the queue intact, and display the stall honestly at both ends
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A permanently stalled seam becomes a terminal state recorded as expired, cancelled, or superseded as applicable, and never as applied
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor runs on what it holds under local gates; the record shows exactly what is known; the audit records the stall
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Captures fold in inside the finish window flagged late_arrival; after finish, audited recompute; commands reconcile on acknowledgement

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A Command Center action cannot be executed: the owning service refuses, is unavailable, or the write succeeds but the read-back fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: On refusal show the refusal and its reason; on unavailability show that the action could not be taken and that nothing changed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the owning service remains unavailable, no action of that class can be taken from any surface, including the Hub's own screens
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No local state, no assumed state, no action; the floor is unaffected and continues under its local deterministic layer
failures_fallbacks.recovery: None on the Command Center, because it holds nothing; the owning record is authoritative and the audit log settles which

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Operational data cannot be created: device unavailable, package undeliverable, envelope cannot compose, or device destroyed with unsynced captures
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reassign or substitute the worker under action 8 so a different qualified worker on a working device performs the capture
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where a device is lost with unsynced captures, those captures are unrecoverable; the run is closed manually with a mandatory note and the gap is recorded
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The record contains what was actually captured and an explicit account of what was not; no fabricated value exists anywhere
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Late captures fold in inside the finish window flagged late_arrival; after finish, audited recompute; reconciliation never invents a capture

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Delivery Operations Hub service is unavailable — total, partial, or the audit write path alone
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry reads on cadence; hold last confirmed state behind an as-of marker; refuse writes with a plain reason
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Render an explicit not-live state and withdraw the action controls entirely rather than disabling them
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Controlled hold on oversight; production continues on pinned packages under local gates; every held item remains held; every frozen lot remains frozen
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Services restore; board refreshes from Hub records; device queues drain in order; pending commands deliver and acknowledge; no Command Center reconciliation is required

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The generator produces one permission view and fails on the other, or a functionality has no row for one of the nine role types
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Publication of the newer view is withheld and the previously published, internally consistent pair remains in force with its own generation timestamp
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Permissions, Roles and Access module renders a banner stating that published permission documentation is unavailable and naming the last known-good version
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Runtime enforcement is never affected; a documentation outage degrades explanation, never enforcement
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The defective row is corrected, the build re-run, both views publish together; decisions taken while stale are re-evaluated in a batch report

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A role card field is left blank, or filled with an invented contractual value where the Statement of Work is silent
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The field is set to `Not specified in the Statement of Work` with a classified proposal, or `TBD — Client Decision Required` with a decision identifier, options, recommendation, trade-offs and owner
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The card renders the field as an open question and the role is marked as not implementation-ready
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A role whose card is not implementation-ready is not provisioned in a production tenant; no role is enabled on an assumed permission
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The decision is taken, the card completed, the role provisioned; pre-production assignments are re-evaluated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A new feature ships with rows for some roles and none for the others, leaving role types undefined at runtime
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The enforcement service applies deny-by-default; an undefined permission is a refusal, never a grant
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the enforcement service cannot resolve the feature at all, the surface renders it unavailable with a named reason and raises a platform alert
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The feature is not reachable by any role until a complete row set exists; no role is silently promoted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rows are authored, reviewed against the absolute rules, published; deny-by-default refusals during the gap are listed for the Tenant Admin

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A condition source is unreachable, the audit writer is unavailable, the decision service times out, or a cached device identity is older than the offline trust window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: An unreachable condition source produces an explicit refusal with a named reason, never an assumed allow (deny-by-default)
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the audit writer cannot commit, the action does not happen; the surface states 'This action could not be recorded and was therefore not performed' and offers a retry
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Read-only posture for the affected capability with an explicit banner; the Frontline device continues local execution and local gate enforcement
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Sources return; three consecutive healthy evaluations exit; blocked actions are retried by their originators, never replayed automatically

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Extends FB-ACCESS-001 with the surface-level degradation states Healthy, Degraded, ReadOnly, Recovering, Reconciling
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Reads served from a short-lived cached decision with a freshness marker; writes refused
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Two consecutive failures inside one minute enter the ReadOnly state with a named banner
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The ReadOnly state with the floor unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Three consecutive healthy evaluations, then a mandatory Reconciling state producing the refusal report before returning to Healthy

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An implementation takes the union first and applies explicit deny afterwards, or takes the union of scopes across all held roles
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The evaluation is rejected and the request refused, because a permission model that cannot be evaluated correctly must not guess
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the role resolver cannot return the held role set, the identity is treated as holding no roles and every request is refused
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The identity's session is limited to reading its own profile with a banner stating that role resolution is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The resolver returns; the session's cached role set is discarded and re-resolved, never reused

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A mirroring write to the tenant audit stream fails, the banner fails to render, the session expiry timer fails, or an End-session press does not take effect
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A failed mirror write refuses the session action; a missed banner heartbeat suspends the session
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the session cannot be suspended cleanly, the session token is revoked at the gateway, terminating every in-flight request
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The session is closed, the tenant's surfaces return to their ordinary state, and a session-terminated event is written to both audit streams with the reason
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The operator opens a new session with a fresh reason and expiry; a failed session is never resumed; action counts in both audit streams are compared

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A code path reaches a protected operation without passing the absolute-rule evaluation, or a rule check depends on an unavailable service and is skipped
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The operation is refused; an absolute rule that cannot be evaluated is treated as violated
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the assertion mechanism itself is unavailable, the protected operations are disabled at the gateway
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Console account creation, role assignment, cross-domain session opening and lot release are unavailable with an explicit banner; Frontline execution continues
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The assertion mechanism is restored and three healthy checks pass; any operation that succeeded without a recorded assertion is a security incident

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A role card field is answered with an invented value, or a prohibition is stated without a source
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The field is converted to `TBD — Client Decision Required` with a decision identifier and a full decision card
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The role is marked not implementation-ready and is not provisioned in production
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No role is enabled on an assumed permission
failures_fallbacks.recovery: As described in FB-ROLE-CARD-001 in section 10.2

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The root's multi-factor device is lost, the allowlist blocks the legitimate holder, the account is compromised, the holder is unavailable, or critical requests accumulate
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Band B operations continue under Admin authority and Band A maker-checker continues under Admin approval; only the critical class and console account creation stall
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the root is unavailable beyond the client's tolerance, the dual-controlled break-glass re-provisioning procedure of section 11.2.3 is invoked
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform continues to operate for tenants; critical-class actions do not occur; tenant execution on the floor is entirely unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The root authenticates or is re-provisioned; the queue is worked; each approval is a fresh human act

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A console action executes without a classification, or is classified more permissively than its content warrants
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: An unclassified action is refused
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the classifier is unavailable, all non-ordinary console actions are disabled at the gateway
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Ordinary Band B read operations continue; every mutating and every tenant-context action is unavailable with a named banner
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The classifier returns and three healthy classifications pass; under-classified actions are treated as security incidents and reported to any affected tenant

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Custodians unavailable, the backend re-provisioning path fails, the atomic replacement partially completes, or the re-provisioning audit event cannot be written
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: If the atomic replacement cannot complete, it rolls back entirely and the previous identity remains active; a partial state is never left
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If rollback also fails, the account store is placed in a read-only posture for console accounts and the incident is escalated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Tenants continue to operate; critical-class actions and console account changes wait; no account created, no role assigned, no invariant touched
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-provisioning completes; the queue is worked as fresh human acts; the exactly-one-root assertion must pass three consecutive times

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No Admin account is available, an Admin approves a change they authored, or the approval queue is unreachable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Platform Engineer changes wait in the queue; they never auto-apply after a timeout
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: If the queue is unreachable, Band A submission is disabled at the gateway so changes are not lost between the maker and the queue
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform runs on its current configuration; tenants are unaffected; no Band A change takes effect
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An Admin account is restored by the root, or the queue returns; three healthy checks exit the state

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The evaluation harness is unavailable, the approval queue is unavailable, or a change applies without a recorded approval
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Where the harness is unavailable, agent-affecting changes cannot be submitted at all; the gate is hard, so an unavailable gate blocks rather than waives
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the queue is unavailable, Band A submission is disabled at the gateway
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform continues on its current configuration; no agent behaviour changes; tenants and the floor are unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The harness or queue returns; submissions resume; nothing is applied retrospectively; an unapproved applied change is a security incident reverted by a fresh approved change

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The banner fails to render, the tenant mirror write fails, the time box fails to expire, an End-session press does not take effect, or an engineer attempts a write
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A failed mirror write refuses the read; a missed banner heartbeat suspends the session
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The session token is revoked at the gateway, terminating in-flight requests
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The session is closed and a session-terminated event with its reason is written to both audit streams
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A new session is opened with a fresh reason; action counts in both audit streams are compared and any discrepancy raised as a finding

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A console screen renders tenant operational content outside a session, or a session frame exposes navigation to a second tenant
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The response is withheld and the request refused
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The session is terminated and the console screen is disabled pending investigation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Tenant-context reach is unavailable across the console; console administration continues
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The defect is corrected and the assertions pass three consecutive times; cross-tenant exposure is treated as a security incident, never as a rendering defect

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A role removal would breach a mandatory-role rule, the identity provider is unreachable, or a worker's cached credential ages past the offline trust window
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A breaching removal is refused with the rule named; the managed-credential path can be pre-provisioned as a documented contingency
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no authentication path succeeds, the tenant's web surfaces are unreachable for affected users; already-authenticated Frontline workers continue inside the offline trust window
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor continues executing on already-assigned runs with cached credentials until the trust window expires; after expiry the worker cannot start new work
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The identity provider returns; sessions re-establish; devices re-authenticate at next connectivity; parked or unstartable runs are listed for the Supervisor

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The last Tenant Admin is removed or locked out, a configuration write partially applies, or the tenant enters soft or compliance suspension
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A breaching removal is refused; a partial configuration write rolls back entirely
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Under compliance suspension all logins are blocked immediately, in-flight runs stop, and devices lock at next contact with the fixed message 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.'
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant's records are intact and unpurged; no configuration is half-applied; no worker loses captured work
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Lockout resolved by another Tenant Admin, or through a support ticket and, where data must change, the compliance-emergency path

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Supervisor is unreachable when a clearance is needed, the worker's device is offline when a clearance is granted, no Supervisor is on shift when an escalation resolves, or a substitution is initiated offline
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: An unacknowledged expiry notification escalates to the Quality Manager after the configurable window, default 2 minutes
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where the clearance cannot reach an offline device, the blocked run parks and the worker continues their other assigned runs
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The worker is not blocked from all work, only from the gated run; no override occurs on the device; no gate is bypassed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The device syncs; the command validates and applies; the run resumes; parked-run durations are reported so repeated parking in one Area is visible
